prompt: A payment consumer restarts during a broker rebalance. The broker stores one event, the new consumer receives it again, and two charges appear. Diagnose and recover without deleting broker data or assuming the broker violated its contract.
directAnswer: Contain the effect first: stop or isolate the unsafe consumer and prevent further charges while preserving broker positions and histories. Bind the source operation ID, stable event ID, topic/queue and partition/position, producer attempts, delivery attempts, old/new consumer generations and assignments, provider idempotency keys/responses, local deduplication/effect records, checkpoints and user outcomes. A likely crash window is that the first consumer successfully charged the provider but died before its acknowledgement or offset checkpoint became durable, so at-least-once recovery redelivered the same stored event. If the second attempt generated a new provider key or had no effect-side deduplication, it created another charge. Reconcile affected users and provider ledger before redrive. Fix by reusing one business operation key across all attempts, persisting an inbox/deduplication record and provider result, making the effect and dedupe atomic where possible, and checkpointing only after recoverable completion. Enforce current assignment generation or another target-side fencing token when overlapping owners can act. Test crashes before effect, after effect, before checkpoint and during rebalance. Broker record deletion and automatic commits would hide evidence or increase loss; neither repairs duplicate external effects.
foundation: At-least-once delivery intentionally redelivers when acknowledgement is uncertain. Exactly-once broker mechanisms do not automatically include an external payment provider. Stable identity, effect-side idempotency, checkpoint placement, fencing and reconciliation close the business boundary.
reasoningSteps: Contain additional external effects without destroying input evidence.
Trace stable source event delivery effect and checkpoint identities.
Separate duplicate source creation broker append redelivery and external effect.
Reconstruct the crash and rebalance timeline.
Verify whether provider and local idempotency identities were reused.
Reconcile provider ledger source state and affected users.
Implement atomic or reconcilable dedupe/effect handling.
Fence stale assignments at the effect owner where required.
Fault-test every crash window and validate user outcomes.
seniorAnswer: I do not call this a broker duplicate until I classify the identity chain. One stored event redelivered after a lost acknowledgement is expected at-least-once behavior. I contain charges, reconcile users, preserve positions, then make the provider effect idempotent under one stable operation ID, persist its result, checkpoint after recovery is durable and fence stale owners. I prove the fix by crashing at every boundary and verifying one provider effect plus correct progress.
weakAnswer: Kafka delivered twice. Enable exactly once, commit offsets automatically, and delete the duplicate event.
whyWeak: The broker stored one record and redelivered after uncertainty; automatic commits can lose effects, deletion destroys evidence, and broker-scoped exactly-once does not automatically cover the payment provider.

evidence.signal: source operation event ID and broker positions
evidence.proves: whether source or broker stored one logical record

followUps.prompt: What if two broker records have different event IDs?
followUps.answer: Trace source/outbox and producer retry creation; two IDs represent a publication-identity failure that effect idempotency may still contain but source construction must be fixed.

followUps.prompt: Can a transaction between Kafka input and Kafka output solve this?
followUps.answer: It can atomically bind broker input positions and broker outputs inside the documented Kafka boundary. The external payment still needs its own idempotency and reconciliation.

followUps.prompt: Why add fencing if idempotency exists?
followUps.answer: Idempotency prevents the same operation from applying twice, while fencing also prevents a revoked owner from applying stale or later conflicting work under a different operation.

rubric.observableEvidence: Unsafe effect stopped without deleting input
Source event delivery effect checkpoint and generation bound
Stable idempotency effect durability checkpoint and fencing
